paper_title: Constraints on hidden photons produced in nuclear reactors
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing epsilon (dimensionless); y-axis plotted as Log10(epsilon), values converted to linear epsilon
notes: Paper derives a revised 95% CL upper limit on hidden photon kinetic mixing epsilon vs mass mX from published TEXONO reactor data, correcting Park (2017) by including photon-hidden photon oscillations in matter (effective photon mass m_gamma ~ 20 eV) and the anti-Compton selection efficiency. The result is only shown in Fig. 1 (no numerical table). Data points here are reconstructed from the physics described in the text: for mX >> 20 eV the limit is a factor ~4^(1/4)~1.4 weaker than Park's ~1e-5, giving epsilon ~ 1.5e-5 (flat up to the kinematic production cutoff at mX ~ MeV); for mX < 20 eV the signal scales as (mX/m_gamma)^8 in epsilon^4, so the limit degrades as (m_gamma/mX)^2, losing sensitivity entirely below mX ~ 0.1 eV as stated in the abstract. Point values are approximate reconstructions, not digitized from the figure, hence moderate extraction confidence.
